Like other event maps, this map had a specialized wave structure with special enemies. Players started with a varying amount of cash, based on how many players there were in the match. The rewards received were based on how many waves were survived and if the match was won. This map had two difficulties, Easy and Hard. Cash is only gained if an enemy was killed, or in some cases, damaged by a specific amount of health. Additionally, the amount gained was a set amount of cash, which was not always equal to the enemy's health. Enemies split their cash between players, regardless of how much damage the player dealt to it. If, in a duo, one player did all the damage to an enemy, both players would receive 50% of the cash the enemy would normally give in solo. This means that in solo, you received 100% of the cash when an enemy is killed, or it was damaged enough. With each additional player, this is reduced to 50% in duo, 33% in trio and 25% in quad. If it was a decimal, it gets rounded up or down depending on the decimal value. If it is at least 0.5, it gets rounded up. If it is less than 0.5, it gets rounded down. Health of enemies in this mode scaled with player count and difficulty. *In Easy, the increase was 20% in duo, 40% in trio and 60% in quad. *In Hard, the increase was 15% in duo, 30% in trio and 40% in quad. In the Hard difficulty, [[Skills]] became disabled. Base health was set to 100. The final boss of this map was the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]]. ==Design & Path== '''The Narratorium''' was a giant theater located in a military base. It consisted of three areas. The first and largest was the audience. This contained multiple rows of seats, most of which were taken up. Some of the rows were taken up by cardboard cutouts of an audience, ones next to [[Lord Exo]]'s throne were taken up by users from the player's friend list while the ones on the side of the stage were taken up by the game developers. The second largest area was the playable area, which contained a recreation of the various stages of the [[Old World]], Paradise and [[Overworld]]. In front of this, there was a stage which showcases various cardboard cutouts that change as the waves progress. Every tenth wave, the playable area would change, giving it a different look. This, however, had little actual impact on the gameplay. The stage itself also changed seven times. Four [[Spotlight]]s were placed on the edges of the stage, which on the final wave are used to stun the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]]. The path started at the stage and ends at the control panel. There were two paths total in the Easy difficulty and four in Hard. ==Interactive Map== {{Map:The Narratorium}} ==Preset Loadouts== Each player was allowed to pick from one of three preset loadouts in each difficulty. Alongside these preset options, players could opt to use their current loadout as the first choice. ==Strategy== *Towers are best placed around the middle of the map, due to it being the closest to all four paths and near a cliff spot, where if [[Ranger|Rangers]] of level 2 or greater were placed down, surrounding towers could get a range buff at the beginning of each wave. *Due to the left most and right most paths being far away from most ideal tower spots, high range DPS towers are recommended here. This includes towers like the [[Ranger]], [[Turret]], [[Accelerator]], [[Warlock]] or [[Pursuit]]. **This is far less of an issue on the Easy difficulty, as the two most problematic paths are not used there. **The [[DJ Booth]] and [[Ranger]] can both be used to boost the range of your towers. However, the range buff from the [[Ranger]] is only temporary. *On the final wave, the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]] is capable of dealing damage to the base health, specifically 40% of the base health and all [[Medic]] overheal. **To prevent the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]] from dealing any damage, players have to aim all the [[Spotlight]]s at it. The spotlight can be set in place by clicking or hovering on the spot you want it to aim at. It is possible for one player to aim multiple spotlights at once. **In the Easy difficulty, it is possible to completely ignore this mechanic, as you can kill the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]] quickly enough for the damage to not matter. ***This is even more true with [[Skills]], as the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]]'s base damage does not account for overheal, meaning that with fully upgraded [[Skills]], the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]] has to use its ability eight times to end the match instead of the usual three. ****This is however not advised, as while performing this ability the [[Narrator (Enemy)|Narrator]] becomes immune to damage, meaning that while you can pay no attention to the match and still win, using the [[Spotlight]]s will make the match end sooner. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Thumbnails}} TheFinalActPromoImage.png|'''The Narratorium''' on the game thumbnail. {{GalleryHeader|Promotional Images}} TheFinalActPI3.png|'''The Narratorium''' on a promotional image. Organization|T.D.S.]] Base }} ==Trivia== *'''The Narratorium''' is the first map in the game since [[Krampus Frosthold]] to change stages when reaching a certain point in the match. **However, unlike all previous uses of this feature, towers are not sold when the stages are switched. *'''The Narratorium''' is the only map to include preset loadouts for the Hard difficulty, most likely because of a collaboration between Tower Defense Simulator and ''Forsaken''. **Having the badge for beating this map on the Hard difficulty also gives the player the Narrator Noli skin in ''Forsaken''. ***The Narrator Noli skin in ''Forsaken'' can still be earned by beating [[Hardcore Mode|Hardcore]] mode. **This is also the second collaboration Tower Defense Simulator has had with another game, with the first one being the [[Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event]]. *This map's pathway has a somewhat similar concept to that of [[Krampus Frosthold]], particularly in the beginning of the map; however, the end paths are all close to each other rather than being far apart. *This map takes place on either Monday or Friday as the opening cutscene shows the [[Accelerator]] preparing to eat a hamburger.
